name: MonarchAiTableAnswer
title: AiTableAnswer
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll Row of cells sized with androidx.compose.ui.text.TextMeasurer, with MonarchCopyButton, MonarchButton and MonarchSkeleton
summary: A table the model produced, shown as a real table: column types inferred, sortable headers, Copy as CSV, an optional Open as artifact, and rows that can stream in.
whenToUse: In an assistant reply whose answer is tabular, for example a tool's rows or a comparison the model built, so people can sort it, copy it and open it at full size.
whenNotToUse: For the app's own records with selection, filtering and paging use the data table components. For a few numbers in a sentence use text with MonarchTabularNumber.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiTableAnswer(rows: List<Map<String, MonarchAiJSON>>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, columns: List<MonarchAiTableColumn>? = null, streaming: Boolean = false, sortable: Boolean = true, copyable: Boolean = true, visibleRows: Int = 200, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiTableAnswerLabels = MonarchAiTableAnswerLabels(), onOpenAsArtifact: (() -> Unit)? = null)
data class MonarchAiTableColumn(key: String, label: String? = null, type: MonarchAiTableColumnType? = null, alignment: MonarchAiTableColumnAlignment? = null)
enum class MonarchAiTableColumnType { Text, Number, Date }

class MonarchAiTableAnswerLabels(aiTable: String? = null, rowCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, copyCsv: String? = null, copied: String? = null, openAsArtifact: String? = null, sorted: ((column: String, ascending: Boolean) -> String)? = null, sortState: ((ascending: Boolean) -> String)? = null, empty: String? = null, noRows: String? = null, loadingRows: String? = null, complete: String? = null, showAllRows: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows, as the conversation model's JSON values, for example a tool's output.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the table answer.

options.name: title
options.description: The title under the AI table label.

options.name: columns
options.description: Order, headers, types and alignment. null makes a column of every key, in the order the keys first appear, with inferred types.

options.name: streaming
options.description: Rows are still arriving: a placeholder row, Open as artifact disabled, and "Table complete." announced when it turns false.

options.name: sortable
options.description: Whether the headers sort the table.

options.name: visibleRows
options.description: Rows drawn before Show all rows. Sorting and the CSV use every row.

options.name: icon
options.description: An AI glyph before the label, in the AI strong color. Monarch bundles no icons.

states.name: unsorted
states.description: Rows in the order the model gave; every header shows two subtle chevrons.

states.name: sorted
states.description: The active header draws its direction's chevron strong and reads Sorted ascending or Sorted descending. Blanks stay last.

states.name: streaming
states.description: A placeholder row of skeleton bars under the rows; Open as artifact is disabled.

states.name: empty
states.description: No rows and not streaming: No rows. Copy as CSV is disabled.

states.name: long
states.description: More rows than visibleRows: a Show all n rows button under the table.

appearance: The AI table label in the AI strong color, the title in the subheading style and the row count in muted caption text. The grid has a subtle border and row separators, a header row on the subtle background with muted label text, and default body text in cells; numbers use tabular digits and an empty cell shows a dash in the subtle text color.
platformNotes: Compose has no data table, so the grid is drawn by Monarch, as on iOS: headers are buttons with the heading role and the sort as their state, and each row is one TalkBack element of header and value pairs (the web uses an HTML table with aria-sort). Android's MonarchAiJSON.Object keeps its key order, so inferred columns follow the order keys first appear; iOS sorts them alphabetically because Swift dictionaries have no order. Column widths are measured with a TextMeasurer so rows line up; long cells stay on one line and the table scrolls sideways. The web's per-column render function is not offered; cells are text. Dates are ISO strings shown as given and sorted as UTC when they have no zone. iOS's leading and trailing alignment are Start and End, isStreaming, isSortable and isCopyable drop the is prefix, copyCSV is copyCsv and sortValue is sortState, following Kotlin and Material 3 naming. Monarch bundles no icons, so the sort chevrons are drawn on a Canvas and the AI glyph is a slot. Copy as CSV uses MonarchCopyButton, which writes the system clipboard; Android 13 and later show their own confirmation.
accessibility: The AI table label, title and row count are one heading element.
Each sortable header is a button with the heading role, read as its name with Sorted ascending or Sorted descending as its state, with a 48dp touch target.
A sort is announced through a polite live region, for example "Sorted by Revenue, ascending.".
Each row is one element read as "Region: North, Revenue: 1,200"; an empty cell is read as Empty.
The streaming placeholder is read as "More rows are being generated", and the end of streaming is announced as "Table complete.".
The sort chevrons are decorative; the direction is the spoken state.
edgeCases: Text a spreadsheet would run as a formula (=, +, -, @) is prefixed with ' in the CSV; numbers such as -3 are kept.
Numeric text such as "1,200", "12%" and "−3" sorts by value; mixed columns are text, compared ignoring case and accents with numbers in numeric order.
A date or time without a zone is read as UTC for sorting; an impossible date makes the column text.
JSON numbers in a number column are formatted for the locale; numeric text is shown as given.
Arrays and objects in a cell are shown as compact JSON.
The CSV is rebuilt when the rows or the order change while copyable; very large tables should set copyable false and offer an export.

examples.title: Sortable table
examples.template:
MonarchAiTableAnswer(
    rows = listOf(
        mapOf({{columns.0}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.0.0}}), {{columns.1}} to MonarchAiJSON.Number({{rows.0.1|double}}), {{columns.2}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.0.2}}), {{columns.3}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.0.3}})),
        mapOf({{columns.0}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.1.0}}), {{columns.1}} to MonarchAiJSON.Number({{rows.1.1|double}}), {{columns.2}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.1.2}}), {{columns.3}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.1.3}})),
        mapOf({{columns.0}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.2.0}}), {{columns.1}} to MonarchAiJSON.Number({{rows.2.1|double}}), {{columns.2}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.2.2}}), {{columns.3}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.2.3}})),
        mapOf({{columns.0}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.3.0}}), {{columns.1}} to MonarchAiJSON.Number({{rows.3.1|double}}), {{columns.2}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.3.2}}), {{columns.3}} to MonarchAiJSON.Text({{rows.3.3}})),
    ),
    title = {{title}},
    columns = listOf(
        MonarchAiTableColumn({{columns.0}}),
        MonarchAiTableColumn({{columns.1}}, alignment = MonarchAiTableColumnAlignment.End),
        MonarchAiTableColumn({{columns.2}}, alignment = MonarchAiTableColumnAlignment.End),
        MonarchAiTableColumn({{columns.3}}),
    ),
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Bot, contentDescription = null) },
    onOpenAsArtifact = {},
)
examples.code:
MonarchAiTableAnswer(
    rows = listOf(
        mapOf("Region" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("North"), "Deals" to MonarchAiJSON.Number(42.0), "Revenue" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("1,240,000"), "Last update" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("2026-03-04")),
        mapOf("Region" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("South"), "Deals" to MonarchAiJSON.Number(31.0), "Revenue" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("980,500"), "Last update" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("2026-01-15")),
        mapOf("Region" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("East"), "Deals" to MonarchAiJSON.Number(57.0), "Revenue" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("1,710,250"), "Last update" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("2026-02-20")),
        mapOf("Region" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("West"), "Deals" to MonarchAiJSON.Number(18.0), "Revenue" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("455,000"), "Last update" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("2026-03-11")),
    ),
    title = "Pipeline by region",
    columns = listOf(
        MonarchAiTableColumn("Region"),
        MonarchAiTableColumn("Deals", alignment = MonarchAiTableColumnAlignment.End),
        MonarchAiTableColumn("Revenue", alignment = MonarchAiTableColumnAlignment.End),
        MonarchAiTableColumn("Last update"),
    ),
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Bot, contentDescription = null) },
    onOpenAsArtifact = {},
)

examples.title: Named columns while rows stream in
examples.code:
MonarchAiTableAnswer(
    rows = listOf(mapOf("closed" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("2024-10-14"), "deal" to MonarchAiJSON.Text("Acme"))),
    columns = listOf(
        MonarchAiTableColumn("deal", label = "Deal"),
        MonarchAiTableColumn("closed", label = "Closed", type = MonarchAiTableColumnType.Date),
    ),
    streaming = true,
)
